name: leather
summary: Worn hide as a garment: a boot, a glove, a belt. Soft, close-grained, and not wound round anything.
why: This exists because leather_wrap was being used for it and leather_wrap is not leather.
Its own summary says so - 'a leather cord wound round the tang, in bands' - and its
grain is that winding: a weave at scale 90 with depth 0.55, which puts a hard band every
few millimetres. On a sword grip that is the subject. On a boot, a glove and a robe it is
corduroy, and it was reported as exactly that: the Dark Wizard came out striped from the
knees down and along both arms.
So the difference between the two is the banding and nothing else. Same substance, same
metallic, near enough the same roughness - one has a cord wound round it and one does
not.
Metallic 0.0. A dielectric keeps its own colour and takes a white highlight, where a
metal tints its highlight and has no diffuse term at all. Dark leather left metallic is
black chrome, which is the single most common way MU's flat art goes wrong under a light.
Rough, at 0.74. A little rougher than the grip, because a grip is polished by a hand and
a boot is not. There is no sharp highlight anywhere on either.
The grain is the hide's own, so it is fine, shallow and not directional in the way a
as texture rather than as stripes at any size a garment is drawn at - and depth 0.06
against 0.55, which is the whole of what made the stripes stand out. Kept as a weave
at all is a boot made of rubber.

The grain it was given is gone; see grain_why. It was written as a fine weave and it still striped, which is the thing that finally settled the question - MU's art is painted flat and a garment's folds are already in the sheet.
A cast grain, added after the Bone set showed what a grainless material costs. This file's
own first line calls the surface close-grained and then stated none, which is the gap: a
material with no grain has depth 0, and build_maps scales the whole height field by that
depth before taking the gradient - so it discards not only its own grain but the relief read
out of MU's painting, which is meant to be half of it. Nine built pieces wearing this were
shipping no normal map at all: the whole Leather set and most of the Vine set, with the
stitching and the folds the artist drew reaching the model as colour and nothing else.
cast rather than weave. weave in this library is bands along one axis - it was written for a
cord wound round a tang - and hide is not wound or woven: its pebbling is isotropic, which is
what cast means here, the same reading plaster and rock get.
under the 256 cells a 1024 map can draw, so the numbers mean what they say at the size this
project builds. Depth 0.06 against bone's 0.10 and range 0.08 against its 0.12: leather is
soft, so its relief is shallow and its gloss varies less than a hard plate's.
Scale 60, and it was 160 first. The number is a count of cells across the map, so a larger
one is a finer grain - and at 160 the pitting came out as hard speckle rather than as hide:
on a shield 400 pixels across that is a cell every two or three, which the frame cannot
resolve and the specular breaks up on. Reported as 'pixelated grain, not nice grain'.
Depth is not the lever and was tried: 0.02 against 0.06 is indistinguishable, because what
is wrong is the size of the features and not their strength. Removing the grain entirely
makes the shield perfectly smooth, which is what identified it. 60 is soft on a shield and
still reads as hide on a Leather Armor, which is the other thing wearing it.

Roughness 0.74 -> 0.62, from the bare Dark Knight's bracers in the same Blender pass: the studs and straps were reading as one flat brown, and a modest sheen is what separates oiled leather from bark. Judged with skin and hair in the frame so the three disagree the way the materials do.
grain_why:
A record of the grain that was tried and removed, kept because the numbers matter.

It was a weave, and it striped. MU's body art is painted flat and the folds are already in the sheet - a procedural weave on top of it is relief the game does not have, and on anything larger than a grip it reads as corduroy.

It was tuned twice before it was removed, and the measurement is why. The Dark Wizard's legs came out with a normal map whose horizontal step was 11.43 against a vertical step of 0.50 - a 23 to 1 ratio, which is not texture, it is stripes. That was after the scale had been taken from 140 to 360 and the depth from 0.1 to 0.05, so the parameter being reached for was not the one doing the damage. The Dark Knight's legs measure 0.10 and 0.08 on the same map, flat, because skin declares no grain and never did.

Kept as a field rather than deleted so the numbers that failed are on the record. A grip is the case that wants one - see leather_wrap, where the winding is the subject - and a garment is not.

What brought it back is a different fault and a different kind. The Bone set showed that a material with no grain has depth 0, and build_maps multiplies the whole height field by that depth - so declaring none discards the relief read out of MU's own painting as well, which is meant to be half of it. The folds this note says are 'already in the sheet' were reaching the model as colour and nothing else, on nine pieces.

So the grain above is cast rather than weave. The measurement that condemned the first one was its anisotropy - 11.43 across against 0.50 along, 23 to 1, which is stripes and not texture - and cast has no direction to be anisotropic in. See the check in the commit: the same legs now measure within a few per cent of square.
